paragraphs: NRG Energy, Inc., or NRG or the Company, serves electricity, natural gas, and smart-home technology solutions to approximately 8 million residential customers (comprised of 6 million retail energy and 2 million smart home), in addition to large commercial and industrial, data center, and wholesale customers. Across North America, NRG is redefining customers' experience with energy under brand names such as NRG, Reliant, Direct Energy, Green Mountain Energy, and Vivint. As of December 31, 2025, the Company's core power and natural gas business consists of approximately 12 GW of competitive power generation, primarily in Texas, and a natural gas portfolio that serves approximately 1,900 MMDth annually.

NRG sold 154 TWhs of electricity and 1,857 MMDth of natural gas in 2025, making it one of the largest competitive energy retailers in the U.S. As of the end of 2025, NRG had recurring electricity and/or natural gas sales in 25 U.S. states, the District of Columbia, and 8 provinces in Canada, and Vivint Smart Home served customers in all 50 U.S. states and the District of Columbia. NRG's retail brands, collectively, have the largest share of competitively served residential electric customers in Texas and is a leading business-to-business provider of power and natural gas in North America.

On January 30, 2026, NRG completed the acquisition of the LSP Portfolio, pursuant to the Purchase and Sale Agreement (the "Purchase Agreement") dated as of May 12, 2025. The LSP Portfolio includes 18 natural gas-fired and dual fuel facilities totaling approximately 13 GW of capacity, located across nine states, as well as CPower, a leading demand response platform.

NRG's strategy is to maximize shareholder value by delivering integrated energy and smart home solutions, supported by an owned generation fleet and a diversified supply strategy. The Company generates power and sells electricity and natural gas to residential, commercial, industrial, and wholesale customers in the markets it serves. The Company also provides smart home security and automation services that deepen customer relationships and support long-term engagement. NRG operates a customer-first platform that promotes reliability and affordability amid rapid transformation in the energy sector. The Company is advancing opportunities to meet growing demand, including from data centers, other large load customers, and electrification. This includes (i) demand response and virtual power plants ("VPP"), which help manage costs and improve affordability for customers, (ii) completing the Texas Development Projects, (iii) long-term, contract-backed generation and related infrastructure, supported by strategic partnerships with equipment manufacturers and engineering, procurement, and construction companies, and (iv) increasing capacity at existing facilities. The Company's differentiated model is built to meet North America's evolving needs while delivering affordable, reliable solutions for customers and long-term growth for shareholders. This strategy is intended to generate recurring cash flow, strengthen earnings and cost competitiveness, and reduce risk and volatility.

To effectuate the Company's strategy, NRG is focused on: (i) serving the energy needs of residential, commercial and industrial, and wholesale counterparties in competitive markets and optimizing on additional revenue opportunities through its multiple brands and channels; (ii) offering a variety of energy products and smart home products and services that are differentiated by innovative, value-additive features, premium service, integrated platforms, sustainability, loyalty/affinity programs, and affordability; (iii) excellence in operating performance of its assets; (iv) achieving the optimal mix of supply to serve its customer load requirements through a diversified supply strategy, including expanding its operational capacity to meet growing retail power supply needs; and (v) engaging in disciplined and transparent capital allocation.

The Company's core businesses are the sale of electricity and natural gas to residential, commercial and industrial and wholesale customers, supported by the Company's wholesale electric generation, as well as the sale of smart home products and services. NRG manages its electricity and natural gas operations based on the combined results of the retail, wholesale and generation businesses with a geographical focus. Vivint Smart Home operations are reported within the Vivint Smart Home segment.
The Company's business is segmented as follows:
•Texas, which includes all activity related to customer, plant and market operations in Texas;
•East, which includes all activity related to customer, plant and market operations in the East;
•West/Other, which primarily includes the following assets and activities: (i) all activity related to customer, plant and market operations in the West and Canada, and (ii) other investments;

In Texas, the Company's generation supply is fully integrated with its retail load. This integrated model provides the advantage of being able to supply a portion of the Company's retail customers with electricity from the Company's assets, which reduces the need to sell electricity to, and buy electricity from, other institutions and intermediaries, resulting in more stable earnings and cash flows, lower transaction costs and less credit exposure. The integrated model also results in a reduction in actual and contingent collateral through offsetting transactions, thereby reducing transactions with third parties.
The integrated model consists of three core functions in each geographic segment above: Customer Operations, Market Operations and Plant Operations.

Customer Operations is responsible for growing and retaining the customer base and delivering an outstanding customer experience. This includes acquisition and retention of all of NRG's residential, small commercial, commercial and industrial, data centers and government customers. NRG employs a multi-brand strategy that leverages a wide array of sales and partnership channels, direct face-to-face sales channels, call centers, websites, and brokers. Go-to-market activities include market strategy planning and development, product innovation, offer design, campaign execution, marketing and creative services, and selling. Customer portfolio maintenance and retention activities include fulfillment, billing, payment processing, collections, customer service, issue resolution, and contract renewals. NRG provides energy and related services at either fixed, indexed or month-to-month prices. Home customers typically contract for terms ranging from one month to five years, while Business customers typically contract for terms ranging from one year to five years in length and extended contractual terms are available. Throughout all Customer Operations activities, the customer experience is kept at the forefront to inform decision-making and optimize retention, while creating supporters and advocates for NRG's brands in the market. Customer Operations primarily comprises two end-use customer facing teams: NRG Home, which serves residential customers, and NRG Business, which serves business customers.

NRG sells a variety of products and services to residential and small commercial customers, in a wide variety of sales channels, including retail electricity, energy management, demand response and/or virtual power plant programs, natural gas, and carbon offsets. Home customers make purchase decisions based on a variety of factors, including price, incentive, customer service, brand, innovative offers/features and referrals from friends and family. Through its broad range of service offerings and value propositions, NRG seeks to attract, retain, and increase the value of its customer relationships by enhancing affordability. NRG's brands are recognized for exemplary customer service, innovative smart energy and environmentally-friendly solutions.

headings: Risks Related to the Acquisition of the LSP Portfolio
The integration of NRG and the LSP Portfolio may disrupt or have a negative impact on the Company's business.
Risks Related to the Operation of NRG's Business
Volatile power and gas supply costs and demand for power and gas could adversely affect the financial performance of NRG's retail operations.
The Company's expectations regarding load growth may not materialize.
NRG's costs, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows could be adversely impacted by disruption of its fuel supplies.
Inflation and customer affordability concerns may limit the Company's ability to recover costs, constrain its pricing and reduce market demand for its products and services.
NRG relies on storage, transportation assets and suppliers, which it does not own or control, to deliver natural gas.
NRG relies on power transmission and distribution facilities that it does not own or control and that are subject to transmission constraints within a number of the Company's core regions.
The Company may incur additional costs or delays in the development and construction of new generation projects and may not be able to recover its investments or complete the projects.
NRG may not have sufficient liquidity to hedge market risks effectively.
There may be periods when NRG will not be able to meet its commitments under forward sale or purchase obligations at a reasonable cost or at all.
The Company's consumer product and home services offerings expose it to installation-related damage claims, product liability, insurance limitations, and reputational risk.
Changes in technology may impair the value of, and the attractiveness of, NRG's retail products, smart home products or services, and generation facilities.
Competition may have a material adverse effect on NRG's results of operations, cash flows and the market value of its assets.

Negative publicity may damage NRG's reputation or its brands and negatively impact its business, financial condition, results of operations and ability to attract and retain highly qualified employees.
NRG's business, financial condition and results of operations could be adversely impacted by strikes or work stoppages by its unionized employees or inability to replace employees as they retire.
NRG's failure to manage key executive succession and retention and to continue to attract qualified personnel could adversely affect the Company's financial condition and results of operations.
Risks Related to Governmental Regulation and Laws
paragraphs: NRG's risk factors are grouped into the following categories: (i) Risks Related to the Acquisition of the LSP Portfolio; (ii) Risks Related to the Operation of NRG's Business; (iii) Risks Related to Governmental Regulation and Laws; and (iv) Risks Related to Economic and Financial Market Conditions and the Company's Indebtedness.

The LSP Portfolio is comprised of 13 GW of natural gas-fired generation and dual fuel assets and a demand response platform. The acquisition significantly increases NRG's owned generation capacity and operational footprint. The acquisition is large and complex, and the Company will need to devote significant time and resources to integrating the plants, equipment, personnel, operations, and fuel arrangements with NRG's existing generation, retail and commercial businesses. Any difficulties encountered in the transition and integration process could adversely affect the Company's business, results of operations and financial condition.
Risks that could impact the Company negatively include:
•the difficulty of managing and integrating the LSP Portfolio and its plants, pipelines, interconnection, operations, fuel contracts, and hedging arrangements;
•the potential disruption of the ongoing businesses and distraction of management;

•difficulties in implementing and maintaining uniform processes, systems, standards, controls, procedures, practices, and policies pertaining to commercial, operational, financial, legal, regulatory, and/or accounting matters;

NRG Energy, Inc., or NRG or the Company, serves electricity, natural gas, and smart-home technology solutions to approximately 8 million residential customers (comprised of 6 million retail energy and 2 million smart home), in addition to large commercial and industrial, data center, and wholesale customers. Across North America, NRG is redefining customers' experience with energy under brand names such as NRG, Reliant, Direct Energy, Green Mountain Energy, and Vivint. As of December 31, 2025 the Company's core power and natural gas business consists of approximately 12 GW of competitive power generation, primarily in Texas, and a natural gas portfolio that serves approximately 1,900 MMDth annually.
The industry dynamics and external influences affecting the Company, its businesses, and the retail energy and power generation industry in 2025 and for the future medium term include:

Market Dynamics — The price of natural gas plays an important role in setting the price of electricity in many of the regions where NRG operates. Natural gas prices are driven by variables including demand from the industrial, residential, and electric sectors, productivity across natural gas supply basins, costs of natural gas production, changes in pipeline infrastructure, global liquified natural gas demand, exports of natural gas, and the financial and hedging profile of natural gas customers and producers. In 2025, the average natural gas price at Henry Hub was $3.43 per MMBtu compared to $2.27 per MMBtu in 2024, representing an increase of 51%.

NRG may experience impacts to gross margins due to significant, rapid changes in current natural gas prices, the impact those prices have on power prices, and the lag in its ability to make a corresponding adjustment to the retail rates it charges customers on term and month to month contracts. The Company hedges its load commitments in order to mitigate the impact of changes in commodity prices, and as a result, these gross margin impacts would be realized in future periods until it is able to make the corresponding adjustments to the retail customer rates.
The relative price of natural gas as compared to coal and prevailing power prices are the primary driver of coal demand. Coal commodity prices increased slightly in 2025.

Electricity Prices — The price of electricity is a key determinant of the profitability of the Company. Many variables such as the price of different fuels, weather, load growth and unit availability all coalesce to impact the final price for electricity and the Company's profitability. An increase in supply cost volatility in the competitive retail markets may result in smaller companies choosing to exit the market, which may result in further consolidation in the competitive retail space. paragraphs: NRG Energy, Inc., or NRG or the Company, 提供電力、天然氣與智慧家庭科技解決方案給約 800 萬戶住宅客戶（包含 600 萬戶零售能源與 200 萬戶智慧家庭），並服務大型商業與工業、資料中心與電力批發客戶。在北美地區，NRG 透過 NRG、Reliant、Direct Energy、Green Mountain Energy 與 Vivint 等品牌重新定義客戶的能源體驗。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司核心的電力與天然氣業務包含約 12 GW 的競爭性電力發電，主要位於德州，以及一個服務每年約 1,900 MMDth 的天然氣組合。

NRG 在 2025 年銷售了 154 TWh 的電力與 1,857 MMDth 的天然氣，使其成為美國最大的競爭性能源零售商之一。截至 2025 年底，NRG 在美國 25 個州、華盛頓特區與加拿大 8 個省份擁有持續的電力與/或天然氣銷售，而 Vivint Smart Home 則服務美國所有 50 個州與華盛頓特區。NRG 的零售品牌 collectively 擁有德州競爭性服務住宅電力客戶的最大市佔率，並為北美地區的企業對企業提供電力與天然氣的領導供應商。
NRG 於 2026 年 1 月 30 日完成收購 LSP 範疇，根據 2025 年 5 月 12 日簽訂的買賣協議（"買賣協議"）。LSP 範疇包含 18 座天然氣燃氣與雙燃料設施，總裝機容量約為 13 GW，分佈於九個州，以及 CPower，一個領先的負載響應平台。

NRG 的策略是透過提供整合的能源與智慧家庭解決方案，以最大化股東價值，此策略由自有發電設施與多元化的供應策略支撐。本公司產生電力，並向住宅、商業、工業與電力批發客戶銷售電力與天然氣。本公司也提供智慧家庭安全與自動化服務，以深化客戶關係並支持長期參與。NRG 運作一個以客戶為先的平台，以應對能源產業快速變革中的可靠性與 affordability。本公司正在推動機會以應對成長需求，包括來自資料中心、其他大型負載客戶與電氣化的需求。這包括 (i) 負載響應與虛擬電力廠 ("VPP")，協助管理成本並改善客戶 affordability，(ii) 完成德州開發專案，(iii) 長期、以合約為基礎的發電與相關基礎建設，並透過與設備製造商與工程、採購與建設公司的戰略合作夥伴支撐，以及 (iv) 增加現有設施的容量。本公司獨特的模式旨在應對北美地區的演進需求，同時為客戶提供可負擔且可靠的解決方案，並為股東帶來長期成長。此策略旨在產生持續現金流，強化獲利與成本競爭力，並降低風險與波動性。

為實現本公司策略，NRG 聚焦於：(i) 服務住宅、商業與工業及電力批發對手在競爭市場的能源需求，並透過其多品牌與通路優化額外收入機會；(ii) 提供多樣化的能源產品與智慧家庭產品與服務，透過創新、價值增加功能、高品質服務、整合平台、永續性、忠誠度/親近度計畫與 affordability 區別化；(iii) 本公司資產的卓越運營表現；(iv) 透過多元化的供應策略達成最佳供應組合以服務客戶負載需求，包括擴充其運營容量以應對成長的零售電力供應需求；以及 (v) 進行嚴謹且透明的資本配置。
本公司核心業務為向住宅、商業與工業及電力批發客戶銷售電力與天然氣，並由本公司電力批發發電支撐，以及銷售智慧家庭產品與服務。NRG 根據零售、電力批發與發電業務的綜合結果，並以地理為重點管理其電力與天然氣運營。Vivint Smart Home 運營則歸入 Vivint Smart Home 分部。
本公司業務分部如下：
•德州，包含所有與客戶、廠區與市場運營相關的活動在德州；
•東部，包含所有與客戶、廠場及市場營運相關的活動；
•西部/其他，主要包含以下資產與活動：(i) 所有與客戶、廠場及市場營運相關的活動在西部及加拿大，以及 (ii) 其他投資；
在德州，本公司發電供應完全整合於其零售負載。此整合模式提供本公司能以自身資產供應部分零售客戶電力的優勢，減少與其他機構及中介機構買賣電力的需求，進而使獲利與現金流更為穩定，交易成本更低，信用風險也較小。此整合模式也導致實際與或有擔保品因抵銷交易而減少，進而減少與第三方的交易；
此整合模式包含上述每個地理區段的三個核心功能：客戶營運、市場營運與廠場營運；

客戶營運負責擴大並維持客戶基礎，並提供優質的客戶體驗。這包括取得與保留所有NRG的住宅、小型商業、商業與工業、資料中心與政府客戶。NRG採用多品牌策略，透過廣泛的銷售與合作渠道、面對面銷售渠道、客服中心、網站與經紀人來進行。市場推廣活動包括市場策略規劃與發展、產品創新、方案設計、活動執行、行銷與創意服務，以及銷售。客戶組合維護與保留活動包括履行、發票、付款處理、收款、客戶服務、問題解決與合約續約。NRG提供能源及相關服務，價格為固定、指數或月結。住宅客戶通常簽約期限為一個月至五年，而商業客戶通常簽約期限為一年至五年，並可延長合約期限。在所有客戶營運活動中，客戶體驗始終被放在首位，以指導決策並優化保留，同時在市場中創造支持者與倡導者；
NRG向住宅與小型商業客戶銷售多種產品與服務，透過廣泛的銷售渠道，包括零售電力、能源管理、需求回應及/或虛擬電廠方案、天然氣及碳抵銷。住宅客戶的購買決定基於多種因素，包括價格、激勵措施、客戶服務、品牌、創新方案/功能以及親友的推薦。透過其廣泛的服務方案與價值主張，NRG致力於吸引、保留並提升客戶關係的價值，透過提高可負擔性來實現；

NRG Energy, Inc., or NRG or the Company, 提供電力、天然氣與智慧家庭科技解決方案給約 800 萬戶住宅客戶（包含 600 萬戶零售能源與 200 萬戶智慧家庭），並服務大型商業與工業、資料中心與批發客戶。在北美地區，NRG 透過 NRG、Reliant、Direct Energy、Green Mountain Energy 與 Vivint 等品牌重新定義客戶的能源體驗。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司核心的電力與天然氣業務包含約 12 GW 的競爭性電力發電，主要位於德州，以及一個天然氣投資組合，每年服務約 1,900 MMDth。
影響本公司、其業務與零售能源及電力發電產業在 2025 年及未來中短期的產業動態與外部因素包括：

市場動態 —— 天然氣價格在許多 NRG 操作的地區對電力價格有重要影響。天然氣價格受多種變數影響，包括工業、住宅與電力部門的需求、天然氣供應盆地的生產力、天然氣生產成本、管線基礎設施的變化、全球液化天然氣需求、天然氣出口，以及天然氣客戶與生產者的財務與對衝狀況。在 2025 年，亨利中心的天然氣平均價格為每 MMBtu 3.43 美元，較 2024 年的每 MMBtu 2.27 美元，上漲 51%。
NRG 可能因天然氣價格的重大且快速變動，以及這些價格對電力價格的影響，而面臨毛利率的衝擊，同時也因無法立即調整其對長期與月結合約客戶收取的零售價格而產生延遲。本公司透過對衝其負荷承諾，以緩解商品價格變動的影響，因此這些毛利率衝擊將在未來期間實現，直到本公司能調整對零售客戶的價格。
天然氣相對於燃煤與現行電力價格，是燃煤需求的主要驅動因素。燃煤商品價格在 2025 年略有上升。
電力價格 —— 電力價格是本公司獲利能力的關鍵決定因素。許多變數，例如不同燃料的價格、天氣、負載成長與發電單元可用性，都會影響最終的電力價格與本公司的獲利能力。競爭性零售市場中供應成本的波動增加，可能導致小型公司選擇退出市場，進而導致競爭性零售市場進一步集中。下述表格總結了 NRG 操作的每個主要市場的平均尖峯電力價格。

headings: 與取得LSP組合相關的風險
NRG與LSP組合的整合可能幹擾或對本公司的業務產生負面影響。
與NRG業務運作相關的風險
電力與天然氣的供應成本波動及需求變化，可能對NRG零售業務的財務表現產生不利影響。
本公司對負載成長的預期可能無法實現。
NRG的費用、營運結果、財務狀況及現金流可能因燃料供應中斷而受到不利影響。
通貨膨脹與客戶負擔能力的擔憂，可能限制本公司回收成本的能力，限制其訂價，並降低其產品與服務的市場需求。
NRG依賴其未擁有或控制的儲存、運輸設施及供應商，以提供天然氣。
NRG 依賴其未擁有或控制的電力傳輸與分配設施，且這些設施在本公司核心區域中可能受到傳輸限制。
本公司在開發與建設新發電項目時，可能面臨額外成本或延誤，且可能無法回收其投資或完成這些項目。
NRG 可能缺乏足夠的流動性，以有效對沖市場風險。
在某些期間，NRG 可能無法以合理成本或完全無法履行其遠期買賣義務。
本公司之消費者產品與家庭服務業務，使其面臨安裝相關損壞聲請、產品責任、保險限制及聲譽風險。
技術變更可能影響 NRG 之零售產品、智慧家庭產品或服務以及發電設施之價值與吸引力。
競爭可能對 NRG 之營運成果、現金流及資產市場價值產生重大不利影響。
負面宣傳可能損害 NRG 之聲譽或品牌，並對其業務、財務狀況、營運成果及吸引與留住高素質員工之能力產生負面影響。
NRG 之業務、財務狀況及營運成果可能因其所屬之工會員工罷工或停工，或無法因員工退休而更換適當人員而受到不利影響。
NRG 若未能妥善管理關鍵高階主管繼任及留任，並持續吸引具備資格之人才，將可能不利於本公司之財務狀況及營運成果。
與政府規範及法律相關之風險
paragraphs: NRG 的風險因素分為以下類別：(i) 收購 LSP 範圍相關風險；(ii) NRG 事業運作相關風險；(iii) 政府管制與法律相關風險；以及 (iv) 經濟與財務市場狀況及本公司負債相關風險。
LSP 範圍包含 13 GW 的天然氣發電與雙燃料資產，以及需求回應平台。此項收購大幅增加 NRG 自有發電容量與運營範圍。此項收購規模龐大且複雜，本公司將需投入大量時間與資源，以整合該項收購的電廠、設備、人員、運營及燃料安排與 NRG 現有發電、零售及商業業務。若在過渡與整合過程中遭遇困難，可能會對本公司業務、營運結果及財務狀況造成不利影響。
可能對本公司造成負面影響的風險包括：
• 管理與整合 LSP 範圍及其電廠、管線、連接、運營、燃料合約及對沖安排的困難；
• 繼續業務可能受到幹擾，以及管理層的分散；
• 在商業、運營、財務、法律、法規及/或會計事務方面實施與維持統一的流程、系統、標準、控制、程序、作法及政策的困難；
